_about: Party press releases and ministerial releases: the party's or minister's own words, not fact-checked. Headline, date, link and a short attributed snippet only; follow the link for the release. Default display should be equal slots per party (e.g. latest 3 each), with a chronological view second, because large parties issue many times more releases than small ones. Items are kept for 60 days and de-duplicated by URL. Built by tools/releases_update.py.
terms_note: Scoop: headlines, links, dates and the first ~200 characters of Scoop's own teaser are taken from Scoop's public InfoPages and section RSS feeds (https://www.scoop.co.nz/about/rss.html), with attribution to Scoop on every item; release text is not reproduced. Scoop's terms (https://www.scoop.co.nz/about/terms.html, retrieved 2026-10-23; copy in raw/releases/scoop_terms_2026-10-23.txt) license Scoop content 'freely to personal and private users' who attribute Scoop and have 'no commercial purposes' (cl. 3.1), restrict unlicensed use 'in any professional capacity' by organisations including not-for-profits (cl. 3.3), count 'direct linking' and automated extraction as 'use' (cl. 3.3.2) and prohibit unlicensed media-monitoring redistribution (cl. 4). The feeds' own copyright line is 'Scoop Media Ltd and/or its contributors'. This guide is a non-commercial volunteer project showing headline + link + short attributed snippet, which is the use RSS is published for; whether that falls under cl. 3.1 or needs a licence has not been confirmed with Scoop (licensing@scoop.co.nz). The Scoop channel can be switched off with --no-scoop, leaving Beehive and the parties' own newsroom links. Beehive: ministerial releases are Crown copyright; beehive.govt.nz says its content is released under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, but the copyright page could not be re-read by script on 2026-10-23 (it returned a script-only response), so check https://www.beehive.govt.nz/copyright. The copyright in each party release belongs to the party that issued it. Items are never fact-checked: they are the party's or minister's own words.
